# Syllabus AI statement — template

Copy, adjust the bracketed parts, and paste into your syllabus. This is a *starting point* — your faculty's academic-integrity policy always takes precedence. Adapted from the kit's [principles](../principles.html); the per-assignment version is the [assignment AI statement](assignment-ai-statement.html).

---

## Generative AI in [COURSE CODE]: how we'll work with it

**The short version:** this course treats generative AI the way we treat calculators, translators and editors — each task says exactly what is allowed, and you say honestly what you used.

**The five levels** (from the AI Assessment Scale, v2.1). Every assignment in this course names its level for each stage:

| Level | Name | In this course it means |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **No AI** | No generative AI use at all for that part |
| 2 | **AI Planning** | AI may help you plan or brainstorm before you start the real work |
| 3 | **AI Collaboration** | AI may give feedback and suggestions during the work; you decide, verify, and log what you took or rejected |
| 4 | **Full AI** | AI may generate freely; your logged judgment of its output is part of what's graded |
| 5 | **AI Exploration** | Working *with* AI is the task itself |

**How to disclose.** Each assignment ends with a short AI-use statement: which level each part used, which tool, what you kept, rejected or verified, and one thing you learned. A template is attached to every assignment brief.

**What happens at each level.** Levels 2–5 are legitimate when disclosed — you lose nothing for honest AI use at the stated level. Undisclosed use where AI is not allowed is handled under [the university's academic integrity policy — link your policy here]: the concern is the concealment, not the tool.

**Why no AI detectors.** We don't use them: published testing found none accurate enough to base an accusation on (none above 80% accuracy; sharply worse on edited and machine-translated text), and they misfire disproportionately on multilingual writers. Your honest disclosure is worth more than a detector score — and asking questions about your work is always how we resolve doubts.

**Where AI doesn't help you.** The parts of each task that build your capability are marked No AI for a reason. Bypassing them with AI doesn't break a rule so much as skip the practice the assessment exists to certify — and the secure checks (in-class, oral, or written defence) will show it.

**Access and equity.** No assignment requires a paid AI subscription: every AI-permitted level can be completed with free tools or the university's licensed tool [name it]. If you have no AI access, or an accommodation affects any part of this policy (including oral assessments), contact [instructor email / accessibility office] — alternatives are built in, not negotiated case-by-case.

Questions about AI use on a specific task? Ask **before** you submit: [instructor email / office hours].
